sections.st: Materials We Use to Manufacture Your Packaging
leads: Trizen Packaging is a thermoforming packaging manufacturer in Vapi, India. We use PP, PETG, APET, PVC, PVDC, HIPS, ABS, ESD-modified PP and PETG, and recycled rPET to thermoform custom packaging for pharmaceutical, medical device, automotive, FMCG, cosmetics, electronics, and industrial applications.

We are not a plastic material manufacturer or distributor. The materials on this page are the thermoforming-grade plastics we process at our Vapi facility to make your packaging. Understanding which material we use — and why — helps you brief your requirement correctly and ensures the finished packaging meets your product, regulatory, and commercial requirements.

sections.st: 8 Thermoforming Materials — What We Work With at Vapi
leads: Each material has specific properties that make it the right choice for certain packaging applications. Here's what we use and why:

strips.title: PP — Polypropylene
strips.desc: 0.20–8.00mm · Translucent — Our most versatile material. High heat resistance (130°C), living hinge capability, available in medical and food-contact grades. Heavy gauge up to 8mm for industrial enclosures.

strips.title: PETG — PET Glycol
strips.desc: 0.20–4.00mm · High clarity — Preferred for medical device blister components and pharmaceutical trays. Outstanding thermoformability, no stress whitening, ETO and Gamma compatible. Density: 1.27 g/cm³.

strips.title: APET — Amorphous PET
strips.desc: 0.20–3.00mm · Max clarity — Used when maximum optical clarity is the priority. Lowest haze of any thermoforming material we use. BPA-free and Gamma stable. Food-contact grade available.

strips.title: PVC
strips.desc: 0.15–1.00mm · High clarity — Global standard for pharmaceutical blister packaging. We use PVC for oral solid dose pharma blister. WVTR: 3.0–5.0 g/m²/day. Heat-sealable with pharma foil.

strips.title: PVDC
strips.desc: 0.20–0.60mm · High clarity — Used when the drug product requires higher moisture barrier than PVC. WVTR: 0.5–2.0 g/m²/day. For moisture-sensitive and hygroscopic pharmaceutical products.

strips.title: HIPS — High Impact PS
strips.desc: 0.50–5.00mm · Opaque/Matte — Cost-efficient structural material we use for industrial trays and enclosures where clarity is not required. Max use temperature 70–80°C. Density: 1.04 g/cm³.

strips.title: ABS
strips.desc: 1.00–6.00mm · Premium finish — Used for premium industrial enclosures and structural panels. Surface finish comparable to injection moulding at thermoforming tooling cost. Max use temp 80–100°C.

strips.title: ESD PP / PETG
strips.desc: 0.30–3.00mm · ESD controlled — Used for electronics and automotive sensor packaging where static discharge would damage the product. Antistatic (10⁸–10¹² Ω/sq) or conductive (10⁴–10⁶ Ω/sq) grade.

sections.st: Why the Right Material Choice Matters for Your Packaging

strips.title: 01. Wrong Material = Product Failure
strips.desc: Using standard PVC for a hygroscopic drug product that needs PVDC or Alu-Alu will result in product degradation before shelf-life expires. Using HIPS for a medical device tray fails regulatory review. We identify and recommend the correct material grade as part of the packaging brief — included in our standard service, no extra cost.

strips.title: 02. Material Drives Compliance Documentation
strips.desc: For pharmaceutical and medical device applications, the material grade on the COA is a required document in your regulatory submission or supplier audit package. Our three certifications — ISO 9001:2015, GMP, Cleanroom Class 8 — combined with the material manufacturer's COA form the complete documentation set for your supplier qualification.

strips.title: 03. One Brief — Material Confirmed Before Tooling Begins
strips.desc: Submit your product sample, application, and regulatory requirements. We identify the correct thermoforming material, confirm grade availability, and include material confirmation in the design specification before tooling begins. No guesswork at your end.

strips.title: 04. ETO and Gamma Compatibility Is Determined by Material
strips.desc: If your device manufacturer will ETO or Gamma sterilize the packed product, the packaging material must be compatible. We select ETO and Gamma compatible materials (PETG, APET, PP) for medical device blister and tray applications automatically — it is part of our standard design process.

strips.title: 05. rPET for EPR and Sustainability Compliance
strips.desc: If your EPR obligation or brand packaging sustainability commitment requires recycled content, we manufacture your thermoformed packaging using rPET in 30% to 100% PCR content — with PCR chain-of-custody documentation from the material manufacturer included in production batch records.

bottomCta.text: Submit your product sample and application requirement. We confirm the right thermoforming material, production standard, and documentation package — within 24 business hours.

faqs.q: What thermoforming packaging materials does Trizen Packaging use?
faqs.a: Trizen Packaging is a thermoforming packaging manufacturer — not a material supplier or distributor. We use the following thermoforming-grade materials at our Vapi facility to manufacture custom packaging: PP (standard, medical grade, food grade), PETG (standard and medical grade), APET (standard and food grade), PVC (standard and pharma grade), PVDC (pharma grade for high-barrier pharma blister), HIPS (industrial grade), ABS (standard), ESD-modified PP and PETG (antistatic and conductive grades), and rPET (30–100% PCR). The right material for your application is confirmed as part of the packaging design brief.

faqs.q: How does Trizen decide which material to use for my packaging?
faqs.a: Material selection is part of our packaging design brief. Based on your product sample and application requirements, we select material using five criteria: regulatory requirement (pharmaceutical GMP, medical device, food contact, ESD), required moisture barrier (for pharmaceutical blister), clarity requirement, gauge and structural requirement, and any sustainability/recycled content obligation. Material selection is confirmed in writing before tooling begins.

faqs.q: What is a material COA and who issues it?
faqs.a: A Certificate of Analysis (COA) is issued by the plastic material manufacturer confirming material identity, grade specification, and batch test results. For regulated pharmaceutical GMP and medical device production batches, we obtain the COA from the material manufacturer for every production run and include it in the documentation package we provide to you. We obtain and pass the COA — the COA is issued by the plastic material manufacturer, not by Trizen Packaging.

faqs.q: Which materials are ETO and Gamma sterilization compatible?
faqs.a: ETO compatible materials we use: PP, PETG, APET, PVC, PVDC, ESD-modified PP and PETG. Gamma stable materials we use: PP, PETG, APET, ESD-modified PP and PETG. For medical device packaging requiring both ETO and Gamma compatibility, we use PETG or PP. PVC and PVDC are not used for gamma-sterilized medical device packaging.
